description: Extend the existing material and narrative physicality authorities with authored forest, tree, height, rope-anchor, and compound-sack consequences without adding globals

replacements.new:
<ROUTINE NARRATIVE-SPILL-SACK-CONTENTS-TO (DEST "AUX" ITEM)
    <REPEAT ()
       <SET ITEM <FIRST? ,SANDWICH-BAG>>
       <COND (.ITEM <MOVE .ITEM .DEST>)
             (T <RETURN>)>>
    <RTRUE>>

<ROUTINE NARRATIVE-SPILL-SACK-CONTENTS ()
    <NARRATIVE-SPILL-SACK-CONTENTS-TO ,HERE>
    <RTRUE>>

<ROUTINE FOREST-IMPACT-DEST ()
    <COND (<EQUAL? ,HERE ,UP-A-TREE> <RETURN ,PATH>)>
    <RETURN ,HERE>>

<ROUTINE FOREST-BREAK-CONTAINED-BOTTLE ("AUX" (WET <>))
    <COND (<NOT <IN? ,BOTTLE ,SANDWICH-BAG>> <RFALSE>)>
    <COND (<IN? ,WATER ,BOTTLE>
           <SET WET T>
           <REMOVE-CAREFULLY ,WATER>)>
    <REMOVE-CAREFULLY ,BOTTLE>
    <COND (.WET
           <TELL "Something inside the sack answers with the unmistakable crack of breaking glass, followed by a brief wetness that the fabric fails to preserve." CR>)
          (T
           <TELL "Something inside the sack answers with the unmistakable crack of breaking glass. The bottle has not survived the experiment." CR>)>
    <RTRUE>>

<ROUTINE FOREST-SACK-IMPACT (DEST "AUX" (HAD-CONTENTS <>) (EGG-BROKE <>))
    <COND (<FIRST? ,SANDWICH-BAG> <SET HAD-CONTENTS T>)>
    <FOREST-BREAK-CONTAINED-BOTTLE>
    <COND (<IN? ,EGG ,SANDWICH-BAG>
           <SET EGG-BROKE T>
           <BAD-EGG>)>
    <MOVE ,SANDWICH-BAG .DEST>
    <COND (.EGG-BROKE
           <TELL "A smaller, expensive-sounding crunch follows from inside the sack. The jewel-encrusted egg has become the canonical broken version of itself." CR>)>
    <COND (<AND <FIRST? ,SANDWICH-BAG>
                <OR <FSET? ,SANDWICH-BAG ,RMUNGBIT>
                    <AND <FSET? ,SANDWICH-BAG ,OPENBIT>
                         <NOT ,MATERIAL-SACK-CINCHED>>>>
           <NARRATIVE-SPILL-SACK-CONTENTS-TO .DEST>
           <TELL "The sack's open geometry declines to remain theoretical; the surviving contents tumble out where it lands." CR>)
          (<AND .HAD-CONTENTS <FIRST? ,SANDWICH-BAG>>
           <TELL "The sack lands with whatever survived the impact still inside." CR>)>
    <RTRUE>>

<ROUTINE FOREST-SHATTER-BOTTLE ("AUX" (WET <>))
    <COND (<IN? ,WATER ,BOTTLE>
           <SET WET T>
           <REMOVE-CAREFULLY ,WATER>)>
    <REMOVE-CAREFULLY ,BOTTLE>
    <TELL "The glass bottle strikes the trunk squarely and ceases to be a bottle. Glass snaps against bark with a hard, bright crack.">
    <COND (.WET <TELL " Water darkens the roots briefly before the game resumes its usual disdain for puddles.">)>
    <CRLF>
    <RTRUE>>

<ROUTINE FOREST-BREAK-EGG-AT (DEST)
    <MOVE ,EGG .DEST>
    <TELL "The jewel-encrusted egg meets the tree with an expensive little crack and falls below seriously damaged." CR>
    <BAD-EGG>
    <RTRUE>>

<ROUTINE FOREST-THROW-NEST-AT (DEST)
    <MOVE ,NEST .DEST>
    <COND (<IN? ,EGG ,NEST>
           <MOVE ,EGG .DEST>
           <TELL "The nest clips the trunk, twists in the air, and throws the jewel-encrusted egg free. The egg reaches the ground in substantially worse condition than the nest." CR>
           <BAD-EGG>)
          (T
           <TELL "The nest brushes the trunk, sheds a few offended twigs, and drops to the ground." CR>)>
    <RTRUE>>

<ROUTINE FOREST-CONSEQUENCE-HOOK ("AUX" DEST)
    <COND (<NOT <FOREST-ROOM?>> <RFALSE>)>
    <SET DEST <FOREST-IMPACT-DEST>>
    <COND
      (<AND <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,FOREST> <VERB? EXAMINE>>
       <TELL "Pines and hemlocks crowd the light into narrow green shafts. Trunks overlap into distance, roots lift the path in places, and the undergrowth is thick enough to make every unmarked direction look like a bad proposal." CR>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,FOREST> <VERB? SMELL>>
       <TELL "The forest smells of resin, damp earth, old needles, bark, and the cooler vegetal air beneath the canopy." CR>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,FOREST> <VERB? LISTEN>>
       <TELL "Needles whisper overhead, branches answer one another in the moving air, and somewhere beyond sight a bird contributes an occasional opinion." CR>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,TREE> <VERB? EXAMINE>>
       <COND (<EQUAL? ,HERE ,PATH>
              <COND (<FSET? ,TREE ,RMUNGBIT>
                     <TELL "The large tree at the edge of the path carries a fresh scar through its bark. Low branches still offer the same climb, and the trunk remains overwhelmingly more tree than lumber." CR>)
                    (T
                     <TELL "The tree is old enough to have acquired weight, rough bark, exposed roots, and several broad low branches. One of those branches offers a plausible way upward without making the tree look remotely portable." CR>)>)
             (T
              <TELL "The nearest trees are mature pines and hemlocks with rough trunks, high interlocking branches, and roots disappearing beneath needles and undergrowth." CR>)>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,TREE> <VERB? RUB>>
       <TELL "The bark is ridged, dry in the raised places, and cool where shadow has held against the trunk." CR>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,TREE> <VERB? SMELL>>
       <TELL "Close to the trunk, resin and bark sharpen the broader smell of the forest." CR>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,TREE> <VERB? LISTEN>>
       <TELL "The tree answers mainly in leaves, needles, small creaks, and the occasional dry complaint of one branch against another." CR>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,TREE> <VERB? KICK>>
       <TELL "You kick the tree. The trunk responds with a deep wooden thud; your foot supplies the more immediate rebuttal." CR>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,TREE>
            <VERB? CUT MUNG ATTACK>
            ,PRSI
            <MATERIAL-DESTRUCTIVE-IMPACT? ,PRSI>>
       <COND (<EQUAL? ,HERE ,PATH>
              <FSET ,TREE ,RMUNGBIT>
              <TELL "The " D ,PRSI " bites through bark and raises a pale wound in the wood beneath. The tree is genuinely damaged and not remotely converted into a convenient pile of lumber." CR>)
             (T
              <TELL "The " D ,PRSI " bites into the nearest trunk and leaves a small raw scar. The surrounding forest does not interpret this as a request to become passable." CR>)>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <VERB? THROW> ,PRSI
            <EQUAL? ,PRSI ,TREE>
            <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,SANDWICH-BAG>>
       <COND (<FIRST? ,SANDWICH-BAG>
              <TELL "You put your shoulder into the throw. The loaded brown sack strikes the trunk with a heavy, fabric-muted thump." CR>)
             (T
              <TELL "The empty brown sack sails with more enthusiasm than authority, slaps the bark, and begins to collapse around its own lack of mass." CR>)>
       <FOREST-SACK-IMPACT .DEST>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <EQUAL? ,HERE ,UP-A-TREE>
            <VERB? THROW DROP>
            <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,SANDWICH-BAG>
            <NOT ,PRSI>>
       <COND (<FIRST? ,SANDWICH-BAG>
              <TELL "You release the loaded sack from the branch. Ten feet of gravity turns an ordinary container into a compact argument about momentum." CR>)
             (T
              <TELL "You release the empty sack. It flutters downward with considerably less commitment than you do." CR>)>
       <FOREST-SACK-IMPACT ,PATH>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <VERB? THROW> ,PRSI
            <EQUAL? ,PRSI ,TREE>
            <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,BOTTLE>>
       <FOREST-SHATTER-BOTTLE>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <EQUAL? ,HERE ,UP-A-TREE>
            <VERB? THROW DROP>
            <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,BOTTLE>
            <NOT ,PRSI>>
       <TELL "The bottle drops through the branches and meets the path below with all the resilience expected of glass." CR>
       <FOREST-SHATTER-BOTTLE>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <VERB? THROW> ,PRSI
            <EQUAL? ,PRSI ,TREE>
            <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,EGG>>
       <FOREST-BREAK-EGG-AT .DEST>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <EQUAL? ,HERE ,UP-A-TREE>
            <VERB? THROW DROP>
            <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,EGG>
            <NOT ,PRSI>>
       <TELL "You let the jewel-encrusted egg discover whether craftsmanship can negotiate with gravity." CR>
       <FOREST-BREAK-EGG-AT ,PATH>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <VERB? THROW> ,PRSI
            <EQUAL? ,PRSI ,TREE>
            <EQUAL? ,PRSO ,NEST>>
       <FOREST-THROW-NEST-AT .DEST>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <EQUAL? ,HERE ,UP-A-TREE>
            <VERB? THROW>
            <NOT ,PRSI>>
       <MOVE ,PRSO ,PATH>
       <TELL "The " D ,PRSO " drops through the branches and comes to rest on the Forest Path below." CR>
       <RTRUE>)
      (<AND <VERB? THROW> ,PRSI <EQUAL? ,PRSI ,TREE>>
       <MOVE ,PRSO .DEST>
       <TELL "The " D ,PRSO " strikes bark, loses the argument, and drops nearby." CR>
       <RTRUE>)>
    <RFALSE>>

<ROUTINE NARRATIVE-PHYSICALITY-HOOK ()
